Glenwood homes listed and sold, June to October 2026

Glenwood, October 2026. Detached houses: 35 listed at month end and 1 sold in October, a sales ratio of 3% (a buyers’ market). Condos and townhomes: 38 listed at month end and 16 sold in October, a sales ratio of 42% (a sellers’ market).

The monthly write-ups singled out Glenwood for detached houses in June, August, September, October (a buyers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in July, October (a sellers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in June (a buyers’ best bet).
Glenwood share of Port Coquitlam listings and sales by month

In Glenwood, its share of the houses listed in Port Coquitlam went from 23.3% in June to 25.5% in October and its share of the condos and townhomes listed went from 18.3% to 17.4%. A share that holds steady while the city moves means the community is following the city; a share that drifts means it is moving differently.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Glenwood PQ
What trades here

items.t: Fee-simple lots — the default form: single-detached homes sit under RS1, RS2, RS3 and RS4 zones in Port Coquitlam Zoning Bylaw No. 3630, with minimum lot widths of at least 15 m (RS1), 12 m (RS2), 30 m (RS3) and 9.5 m (RS4) — zone minimums AS THE RESEARCH STATES THEM. Typical Glenwood lot dimensions: Not verified, so no typical size is carried. A fee-simple lot carries no strata corporation, no Form B and no strata fees. - Zoning Bylaw 2008.pdf
Bare-land strata position: no bare-land strata development offered as vacant lots is verified for this ground.
Age-position guardrail: Do not confuse it with Shaughnessy Park (the Glenwood townhouse complex above) or Shaughnessy Square. Glenwood itself verifies ZERO 55+ ownership stock.
No manufactured-home park: NO manufactured-home park exists in Port Coquitlam in any source — there is no pad-tenure product on this ground, and no park is invented or imported here.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Glenwood PQ

items.t: Glenwood is not named as an established neighbourhood in the City's Official Community Plan — it sits inside the City's north-side residential area — and its boundary roads are not verified: no City neighbourhood map defining Glenwood's boundaries was found on an official source.

Where it sits: north Port Coquitlam, between Lougheed Highway to the south and the Citadel / Oxford Heights area to the north and east; nearby areas are Citadel PQ and Oxford Heights (north/east), Lincoln Park (east), Central Pt Coquitlam (south across Lougheed Highway) and Coquitlam (west). Lougheed Highway runs along the south side, with Coast Meridian Road and Lincoln Avenue as north–south routes.
Sub-area medians are not verified — SnapStats publishes medians at community level only.

A significant portion of Port Coquitlam is within the Fraser and Pitt River floodplain protected by dykes; Glenwood sits on the north side and lot-level floodplain status is not verified, checked with the City. No ALR land was confirmed inside Glenwood. - Zoning Bylaw 2008.pdf

Schools (SD43 Coquitlam, Ministry-listed names): Glen Elementary School (3064 Glen Drive) is the school inside the sub-area. Catchments are address-based — any other address is not verified without its own locator run.

Parks, recreation and transit: the City Parks Directory lists north-side parks including Evergreen Park at 3500 Cedar Drive; Hyde Creek Recreation Centre at 1379 Laurier Avenue is the north-side recreation centre, and the Terry Fox Library is at the Port Coquitlam Community Centre, 2150 Wilson Avenue. TransLink buses connect north Port Coquitlam with Coquitlam Central Station (Millennium Line Evergreen Extension and West Coast Express) and Port Coquitlam Station (West Coast Express); specific route numbers through Glenwood are not verified. Driving commute times: Not verified.

Health and shopping: the nearest hospital is Eagle Ridge Hospital, 475 Guildford Way, Port Moody (Fraser Health), with Royal Columbian Hospital in New Westminster the next larger hospital. No shopping centre or grocery store location serving this sub-area was verified on an official source: Not verified.
How people search for it: "Glenwood Port Coquitlam," "Glenwood PoCo." No other official alternate name was confirmed: Not verified.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Glenwood PQ

items.t: OCP — City of Port Coquitlam Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 3838, which governs the area; no Glenwood-specific plan or major project was confirmed.

Zoning — Port Coquitlam Zoning Bylaw No. 3630: single-detached homes under RS1–RS4 (minimum lot widths at least 15 m / 12 m / 30 m / 9.5 m respectively); townhouse zones RTh1, RTh2 and RTh3 exist in the bylaw. Any parcel's actual zone: per-parcel with the City. - Zoning Bylaw 2008.pdf

Subdivision and servicing — Port Coquitlam servicing bylaw number not confirmed (held, never borrowed): Neighbouring cities' numbers (e.g., Coquitlam 3558, 2003; Surrey 8830, 1986) govern their own municipalities only and are NOT Port Coquitlam numbers. (Standing verified ledger, applied by exclusion.)

Property taxes — City of Port Coquitlam (a municipality; follow its own research): 2026 taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty on current taxes unpaid after July 2, 2026 and a further 5% after September 15, 2026; the City's 2026 increase was 1.95% for the average home, and the City states it has the lowest average property taxes and utility fees in Metro Vancouver. Utility bills are flat annual water and sewer fees, billed separately and due March 31, 2026.

ALR block (applies only where a parcel is ALR — none confirmed inside Glenwood, status per-parcel): subdivision within the ALR requires Agricultural Land Commission approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)). Caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha).

blocks.text: Good to know about Glenwood PQ

items.t: Detached Glenwood was the city's slowest pace that month (Sep 2026). A land buyer pricing a teardown here is pricing off the wider city market, not the street.

Utilities are a separate flat bill with its own deadline (Mar 31, 2026). Port Coquitlam bills water and sewer as flat annual fees separate from property taxes, due March 31 — a second annual deadline a lot buyer used to combined municipal billing misses.

The city claims Metro Vancouver's lowest average tax-and-utility load (2026). The City states it has the lowest average property taxes and utility fees in Metro Vancouver, with a 2026 increase of 1.95% for the average home — a City claim, carried as the City states it.
The sub-area's school anchor is also its locator proof point (Oct 23, 2026).

Three similar names, three different products (Nov 1, 2026). Shaughnessy Park (Glenwood townhouses, 3655 Shaughnessy St), Shaughnessy Square (2099 Lougheed Hwy, counted city-wide in condos) and The Shaughnessy (2789 Shaughnessy St, the city's only high-rise, general-market) are routinely confused in feeds — only the first is Glenwood ground, and none of the three is 55+.

blocks.text: Glenwood home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

45 condos sold in Glenwood with a median price of $512,000 (the middle half sold between $426,000 and $580,000), taking a median of 36 days to sell at 97.1% of the last list price; 4% sold above list. They had a median $576 per square foot, a median year built of 1996 and a median strata fee of $408 a month. 23 houses sold in Glenwood with a median price of $1,300,000 (the middle half sold between $1,129,000 and $1,381,000), taking a median of 27 days to sell at 96.1% of the last list price; 0% sold above list. They had a median $538 per square foot, a median year built of 1973 and a median lot of 6,000 square feet.

faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 35 houses and 38 condos and townhomes listed in Glenwood. Those are month-end counts and they move daily, so ask Jared for a current list.
faq.q: How many homes are for sale in Glenwood?

faq.a: In October 2026, houses had a sales ratio of 3% (a buyers’ market); condos and townhomes had 42% (a sellers’ market). The sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed; on the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers. One month in one community is a small sample, so look at the monthly table above before you decide.
faq.q: Is Glenwood a buyers’ or sellers’ market?

faq.a: 11 houses and 42 condos and townhomes sold in Glenwood over those 5 months; detached houses peaked in July with 4 sold and condos and townhomes peaked in October with 16 sold.
faq.q: How many homes sold in Glenwood from June to October 2026?

faq.a: In October 2026, Glenwood held 25.5% of the 137 detached houses listed in Port Coquitlam and 17.4% of the 219 condos and townhomes listed in Port Coquitlam.
faq.q: How big is Glenwood compared with the rest of Port Coquitlam?

faq.a: In October 2026, houses made up 47.9% of the 73 homes listed in Glenwood and condos and townhomes made up 52.1%; of the 17 that sold, houses were 5.9% and condos and townhomes 94.1%.
faq.q: What mix of houses and condos is for sale in Glenwood?

faq.a: Listings of detached houses fell from 40 in June to 35 in October 2026 (−12.5%); condos and townhomes fell from 42 in June to 38 in October 2026 (−9.5%).
faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in Glenwood than in June?

faq.a: No — it is a board (MLS) sub-area name used in the SnapStats GVR report; the City's OCP does not name Glenwood as an established neighbourhood, and its boundary roads are not verified on any official source.
faq.q: Is Glenwood an official Port Coquitlam neighbourhood?

faq.a: 3 to 6 small-scale multi-unit housing units, depending on lot size, location and transit proximity, per the City's SSMUH position — confirm for the exact lot with the City.

faq.a: Only if a strata plan or a subdivided lot gives that side its own title. An ordinary Glenwood duplex on a single lot sells whole, building and lot together.
